This game isn't so much a game as much as a reminder for me and a very helpful tool for others on what depression is.
In Depression Quest, you are a male in his early 20's who has a girlfriend and a job. he has an apartment, a family, and seems friendly enough. But yet, he has been suffering from a growing sense of unease and dread of who he is and what he is doing. His family seems more successful then him, his girlfriend knows when he is having 'one of those days', and he is miserable at work. He is tired all the time and feels unmotivated to do anything.

There are no easy decisions: There are decisions where it is obvious you should do that yet you can't because it's crossed out. Why? Because you are depressed and unable to do that. From there, you have to make a hard decision on what is the right thing to do for you and you alone.
For someone who has depression and has read up about it, this game is very well researched in terms on what kind of thoughts and choices people like me face. One choice for seeing your co-workers going out to a bar is "Get over it and go out with them" And that choice is crossed out. Those kinds of choices are your brains way of making an extreme and taunting you for not taking that choice, and making you feel rejected enough to not try at all.
For someone who has never gone through depression, it could be difficult. Many of the choices that seem easy enough ( One is to adopt a kitty to have companionship, Saying no due to not feeling ready to take that responsibility, and No because you don't like cats) are actually very hard for someone who doesn't understand how depression works, and might lead to bringing more information to the table.
One of the best things about the game? You fail a lot. You fail to get out of your house that day no matter what, You fail to finish that project, you chose the wrong person. But it doesn't say YOU FAILED TO GET BETTER. It just says...what next? Just like real life.
WOULD I RECCOMEND THIS GAME: YES
This game is a simple 40 minute playthrough that makes you feel depressed. It doesn't go about it by making the parents abusive or making you a fat lazy slob. It does it by stating the simple fact: You have depression, what will you do with it?
SUGGESTIONS TO CREATORS:
Partner up with a mental health organization who can bring this type of game to more people at a low or even free cost. I would love to see even more games like this that deal with other mental disorders or physical illnesses.

This game is important. It's an excellent teaching tool that helps explain what exactly depression is and how it affects those with it. The idea of living a few moments in the life of someone suffering with the condition is handled wih respect and weight, and the choice system is clever. Blocking out the most obvious choices and making the game a challenge based on your depression level is a brilliant use of mechanics to support theme and purpose.
It's a game that wants to show just how many challenges those suffering with depression face in their everyday lives, a teaching tool meant to do away with that hurtful myth about depression being easily beaten with a positive attitude. I honestly think this game's lessons could save lives one day; you need to play through it once, ecause this isn't simply a game. This is an important, heartfelt teaching tool.

If the idea of perfecting your lines, shaving off hundredths of seconds, just to beat that one dude who seems to be topping the list every day, then this is your kind of game.  A casual player need not apply because they simply won't accomplish much.
So what is Musclecar Online? It's a top-down keyboard-controlled racer (which means you need to learn how to engine brake if you're going to do any good here) that features a daily user-made track - and yes, that means they can be quite crazy - with leaderboards for 10 or so different cars, each with their own strengths and weaknesses, though some feel closer to each other than others.  The key point here is that, like Trackmania, it's all about your laptime.  Fastest laptime wins the day.
At first, you will have access to maybe one or two cars and a handful of 'coins'.  This is in-game currency, so no worries about any extra charges.  These coins are used to unlock other cars, but more importantly, their variants as well as the tires they run on, and believe me, if you want to be in the top spot, you'll need to know exactly which variant and what tires you need to run.  Placing a decent time will earn you a silver medal, a great time will earn you gold, and the top spot will earn you an achievement, bragging rights, and possibly the chance to wave your virtual fiddlestick around.  Each possible position silver and above will net you more coins, which will allow you to buy even more cars, more variants, and even a fancy helmet (totally cosmetic).  For the ultimate prize in coins and prestige, win the "daily overall" spot by being the best in the most car classes.  I have no idea what the actual prize for that is because there are TWO SPECIFIC dudes who play this that will make life difficult for you haha
At any rate, it's easy to sink lots of time into this game if you are chasing the top spot because you will need to set the fastest times in the most car classes possible, and that means gradually unlocking all of them and running them on the track for that day.  This can take a significant amount of time if you become obsessed with it.  You might constantly get that feeling of, "I can shave off just a -little- more time on the next lap" and round and round you go (protip: turn off the automatic-end-run option or you might mess up your mojo).
Your opponents?  Other people from around the globe.  I constantly see players from the UK, France, Sweden, and many more.  By 'see', I mean you're not just out there on the track alone; you are racing ghosts (they can be turned off if they are too distracting) and those ghosts are constantly mocking you as you cross the plane just a hair behind them.  The game even features an in-game messaging system so you can send a note to your favorite opponent telling them how much you loathe their face and wish to see it plastered on your car's grill.... *cough*
tl;dr - this is a 2D trackmania and it's incredibly competitive.  If you feel that need to run that perfect, perfect line and edge out the win against other peoples' ghosts, you will find yourself diving down the rabbit hole.  What I thought would be a filler game quickly turned out to be a small obsession and the community is great.

This is game is amazing. I've seen quite a few people saying it's a horrible game because it somehow didn't stick to the old roots of the first game somehow, a game that was made in the 90's. Well, having not played the original, I think I can safely give an opinion of the game, not skewed by memories of the late 90's version.
To start off, I was already a bit biased from the start to an extent, as I love stealth games/stealth features in games. In skyrim, I was always either a mage or a thief, in any rpg game, if I can be a thief, i'll be it, such a fun way to play, sneaking around and hiding in the shadows. So when I heard about this game, I was already excited. It was as good as I expected it to be. The sneak mechanic is pretty well done, although it doesn't have much give when it comes to either being hidden, or being seen, so don't rely on the moon icon too much if you're near people, you have to listen to the sounds to see if someone is discovering you.
Secondly, I love the "staying hidden" options you can do throughout the game, such as extinguishing candles, whether it be snuffing them with your fingers, or dousing them with water arrows. Enemies in the way and no way to get around them? Throw a bottle and distract them so you can sneak around (or maybe even kill, if that's your choice) them.
Thirdly, I love the freeness of the game. Don't wanna focus on the main quests? No problem, go ahead and wander the city, stealing things or even do side-quests. Don't like sneaking a whole lot? just level up your blackjack and get tons of broadhead arrows and go and kill everyone in your way. If you wanna follow the (main) path of the game and be unseen, unheard, unnoticed, everything? build into your stealth options and sneak around like the ghost you are. The game plays out the way you want it to play. Even the difficulties are custom! Sure, there's the easy, medium, hard aspect that normal games have, but you can also make a custom difficulties. Is the hard difficulty not hard enough? No problem, turn off your "focus" ability, make it nearly impossible to stay hidden in the shadows, and make every supply cost 2000 gold. It's a great feature for those people who like to take it to extremes.
Overall, this is a great game. Here are my ratings for it.
for customization
as well for Open-endedness,
for graphics (I didn't feel they needed to be discussed, they're great graphics, they fit good with the game)
for sounds/voice-acting (Also didn't have to be discussed, great voice-acting, Garrett's voice fits so well)
Total: 9.5/10 If you have the money to buy this game, buy it!

This game isn't bad, but is by all acounts mediocre.
Thief is great at giving the illusion of choice; our 'Assassin's Creed-esque' abilities and clever use of aesthetics lead us to believe we can go almost anywhere, but in reality, the game seems to be made up of several pre-designed paths. This quickly becomes apparent when attempting to take anything but the obvious route, and finding that you often have to go through certain bottlenecks regardless. This isn't a gamebreaker, but it is a huge downer.
On the up-side, the range of tools and powers available does make for interesting gameplay, and the choice of how to engage enemies (if at all) is both real and versatile. Combat also seems to find a clever balance between being effective, and yet not being encouraged - this is after all supposed to be a stealth-focused game.
Overall it's like I said in the first line, it's mediocre. It's not particularly pretty, it doesn't have great replay value but if you pick it up for a reduced price, it has a fair few hours of entertainment in it.

I think this is possibly the most polished and coherent first person simulation Ive played. FPSIMs are my favorite game genre, so Im biased to like Thief4 alone for this reason. The previous Thiefs pioneering the FPSIM genre are some of my favorite games (along with Looking Glass' other games), so Im likely to nitpick anything that isnt perfect.
GOOD:
Kind of everything - seriously, I could go on for pages about how well the systems in this game are put together, the level of detail, polish, maps, mechanics, etc. Its astounding.
First person body - special mention, this is wonderfully done. Can all other devs please aim for this bar?
Lighting model (wow, this is one of the best lighting models Ive ever seen used in a game! Just wow.)
Circling mouse to turn wheels
Focus
Options options options: FOV, loot shine, objectives markers, etc (dozens of options)
Custom difficulty - anyone beat the game with a score of 1300?
Removal of jumping - I used to bunny hop round Thief for speed, but it wasnt very thief like, so I appreciate the removal of it. Also it means you dont noisely jump when trying to mantle something. Good call!
BAD:
The name, its "thief 4", not "Thief", Thief came out in 1998. Put a ":some title" in it.
Audio levels seems random (super loud, then super quiet, then super loud - semi random). Sound volume mixing could be greatly improved.
Mantling is awesome, but you cant tell if its possible, or if you are in the right position. Ledges you can jump/mantle to be marked, and highlighted when you are in position. Same for jumping gaps.
Using the "use" key to lockpick for PC users using the mouse to lockpick feels unnatrual. Left mouse click for lock pick (single handed) would be nice.
On multiple play throughs to get loot, its hard to remember where it all is. It would be nice if the map keeps track of loot found
Draws take too long to open and close - it almost feels like its not worth looting them - please speed this up. Or simply remove the animation entirely - please make this optional!
On looting a draw with loot Garretts hand already moves into the looting position when he cant see that there is loot. (Immersion breaker).
Its really hard to find all the loot! It would be nice to have a post story loot finder skill/item to we can track everything down, eg audio cues, thief sense, just shove them all on the map.
Hammering the "use" key is just so ... inconsistent with all the other smooth mechanics. For the love of God please remove the hammering of "use".
Its not obvious where all the city transition points are - city section transition points should be marked on map clearly
Windows that transition city sections need visual identification
Chapter replay points clearly marked on map
Some guards leaning against walls should be blackjack-able
Stats screen is 2 clicks away - hotkey please
Stat changes are mostly silent. Stat changes should always optionally always be posted to gameplay UI, eg challenge status - please add to options screens the stats verbosity level.
Sometimes the map zooms in and you lose context there - in buildings etc map should not remove rest of map and zoom in
Theres only one quick save slot - it would be good to have more eg 5
Quickload key loads the quicksave, not the latest save. Id like it if it loaded latest, thats more natural.
There is a delay after a tumbler is picked before the circle for the next tumbler becomes visible - this slowdown is annoying. It would be good if there was no delay.
The "manual save" system wasnt clearly explained, and I made the mistake of beating the game, looting more things etc (happy days) and then reloading a chapter 3 manual save just for a look about - but I hadnt saved my game manually recently, so I lost 20 hours of progress, because the "autosave" slot got wrote over including my quicksave. Please explain clearly that you have a crazy save system that no one else does, and that each manual save slot is actually a "profile" slot, and the auto-profile slot will be immediately written over. Or just change your save system so its like *every other game*.
UGLY:
Birds - neat idea, frustrating mechanic as its too twitchy!
Lack of amusing guard conversations.
Garretts boring characterisation - he used to be incredibly witty and sarcastic, with loads of intra level commentary.
EDIT: Comparison with Thief (1) Gold. Thief1 has much better writing, loads of sarcasm from Garrett, highly entertaining conversations from guards, etc - its really a joy to listen to. However, the maps are much larger and almost completely empty of clutter/items/etc, and they feel like giant prototype placeholder maps, sketches of ideas, not like a finished product. Theif1s mechanics are not better or worse, they are simply different implementations to Thief4, however, Thief4s mechanics and systems definitely feel more polished, coherent and immersive. All in all, Id like to have everything from Thief4 with the writing and dialogue from Thief1, and if I had to pick one to play forever after at this stage it'd be 2014, its a lot more enjoyable to play. (Ive played Thief1 about a 6 times over the years, but sadly this time Im not really enjoying it. I will persevere because one of my fondest gaming memories was playing Thief1-3 back to back, and I recall the trilogy as a whole was brilliant from a story perspective).

Bunny&Piggy is a platformer that tries to be extremely difficult, makes the theme very cutesie and on a timer, they succeed however just now how they expected it to.
Bunny&Piggy is a platformer where you play either a bunny or a piggy, both squares, however since the levels are so ridiclous its mainly the bunny. Your goal is to collect as much food as possible because "Winter is approaching" and so you jump around frustrating levels trying to collect carrots to exit the level.
The idea of the game is fine, however it is more a browser game then anything. with it's minimalistic 28 levels and an okay yet very repetitive soundtrack it doesnt hold a lot of content you would expect for paying 1 euro. The idea of a hardcore platformer is not new, however it contradicts itsself by going for a cute bunny theme which makes me question what kind of idea's these developers have.
The biggest problem i have with this game is that there is a delay, about 0,2 seconds, between when you press the jump key and when your character jumps; and for a hardcore platformer this is a massive issue. When i play a fast paced hardcore platformer i expect quick responses to be able to coordinate myself quickly and make tight jumps the way i want them to, i do not want to be hinderd by slow and sluggish movement. Because of this issue i can not even make it past the second level since the precise timing to make it across a single gap can not be achieved with this delay in place.
furthermore, according to the store page there are "hard and not-hard levels" however there is no "not-hard" for the average consumer, the learning curve for this game is a straight wall with barbed wire on top. It starts out very difficult and it only gets worse.
On the main menu you can see that there are a variety of languages to choose from, going from english to korean, and this woulndt be a problem until you notice that these have probably been pulled straight through google translate; when changing from English to German instead of the "Hard" and "easy" option translating to be "more difficult" instead it translates to "harder" and "softer" this makes it seem more like the developers added this feature just because they thought they had nothing else to do.
As mentioned in the previous paragraph there is a difficulty option where you can change between "Hard" and "Easy" this barely changes anything besides the time you are given to complete the level and how fast the "enemies" move. i also find this inclusion badly implemented.

Bunny&Piggy is a game that tries to be more then a browser game however its core idea prevents it from doing so and in the end failing at what it was trying to do, create a difficult but playable platformer, instead it's a platformer that can not be played the way it was intended because of it's flaws.

If you liked FC3, then you will probably like FC4. Ubi really upped their game to bring life to the world as there are always things happening around you which can get flat out  ridiculous at times. The sound design is a spectacular step up from FC2 and 3 and it's quite refreshing. There are tons of things to do and explore in Kyrat (sp?) and I already have 13 hours in and have not even gotten past the first 'boss'. Coop is fun but a little jittery, lots of opportunities to have fun and set awesome traps. The game offers much in the way of exploration and has some really awesome side missions to keep you going if you don't want to get through the main campaign too quickly.
On the down side, it feels like Ubisoft is really trying to streamline FarCry in a negative way geared more towards casual gamers. In FC2 and FC3 you would frequently stumble upon some really cool emergent event that would unfold and escalate and generally feel like it was YOU, the player that discovered it and made it happen. In FC4 things don't really happen because you did something. They happen because you are there. After a couple hours into the game, you begin to realize that the soldier you saw pushing a captive through the woods didn't actually "come" from anywhere but had spawned within a 100-150m radius of you.
While understandable from a technical perspective, this type of "random event" becomes very predictable and sort of ruins the immersion. I have literally been in scenarios where six+ karma missions happen consecutively, or simultaneous to eachother. Of couse animals and civillians are also running through the mix screaming and roaring as well.
After a while I sort of feel like the game is trying to shake me out of the narrative slapping me, and saying "HEY YOU'RE DOING REAL WELL THERE BUD LETS SCALE UP THE DIFFICULTY OF THE GAME AT THIS ONE PARTICULAR POINT IN THE WORLD AND SEE WHERE IT GOES FROM THERE!!"
I hope Ubisoft tones the director down a bit because at the moment it clashes very harshly with the story and characters they created.

I think I will finally put out my thought on this game. First off Im sorta♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥about the bad reviews I've seen on metacritic and other places due to the fact that it takes a good PC to run. A lot of people have found "bugs" that is obviousally them trying to run the game on very low without the required settings and are discovering issues due to that. Ok now that I've said that heres MY review
Singleplayer:
The only negative thing is that it is kinda repitive when it comes to the other FC games, beyond that it is fantastic. It keeps a lot from FC3 and adds a whole lot more. The world seems a little smaller, yet. For those who dont know:
Far Cry is an Open world game, meaning that you can go around and do quests, campaign missions unlock more of the map, take outposts and do whatever the hell you want. Its also a First Person Shooter and ties the FPS and OW together very well.
The world of Far Cry 4 takes place in a fictional city called Kyrat, that is located in the Himilayas, you can hunt animals to skin them and craft sacks to carry more of any given item. the game also features enemy outposts where youy can gain an XP bonus for how you take it, the less detected you are, the more XP you get. Now as XP goes I wanna talk about are the skills, instead of 3 groups like we had in FC3, we have 2, Elephant and tiger, Elephant is more defensive whereas Tiger is Attack.  there is no tatoo however ( thank god. it was kinda weird) The quests I havent diven into that much, however there are popup quests around the map as you travel called Karma that will give you Karma XP, which basically as it would suggest, shows how reputable you are with your tribe, Golden Path (Thats what it called right?) If you gain enough XP you can call in troops to help fight with you, however you cant call them in during a mission, which i find sorta annoying.
The next thing is that co op isnt seperate anymore, instead you can aid eachother in single player, mainly to take down the fortressess. Which are like huge, well guarded outposts. Another thing is animals in the game. They are very tough and start to become a quick problem.   However a new feauture can counter this. When you skin an animal, you take its meat and put it in a bait sack, bait is one of your throwable objects, animals will go eat the bait then attack the next thing closest, so you can throw bait into a crowd of enemies to get an animal to attack them. The last thing I wanna talk about is the campaign. I'm not gonna spoil anything, however there are 2 seperate sets of missions after you hit the 6th or 7th missions. So, you can play the game twice and have most of the missions be different.
Multiplayer:
It is amazingly fun.  It is 5v5 and there are 3 different modes. The maps are GIGANTIC! you can use the wingsuit to fly around the map, and the Golden Path can use guns and vehicles, and the enemy act as hunters which are enemies that have bows and can turn invisable. So you get bows and can ride elephants. You also get 2 Special Tipped arrows and you can summon animals to attack the Golden Path. There are usaully 2 10 minute halves depending on the game mode. You are one team for the first half, then switch for the second.
Overall this game is amazing. I HIGHLY reccomend
10/10

I feel the need to write a review for this game since everybody's been hating on it because it's Ubisoft.
Okay, lemme say it straight: Far Cry 4 is an excellent game. There are a lot of improvements gameplay-wise over the last game. The visuals are stunning, the music is excellent, the world is a lot more detailed and immersive compared to the last game.
My only problem is the story isn't as good as the third game's. That's not saying much considering last game's story is one of the best. Despite this, Far Cry 4 still has a large range of extremely interesting and unique characters.
Yes yes yes, Ubisoft hasn't been making a lot of good games lately, but this is a massive exception, and I believe we should support them for their success with this game. Definitely check this out of you loved Far Cry 3.

But, this is one of the few games that is simple enough to get all the achievements, so that's a plus.
The "story" is God-awful. The dialog is cliche, overworn, and extremely annoying, (not to mention some awkward phrasing due to only moderately good translation from Chinese). Your narrator is stereotypically "good" and you are fighting the Talon who is stereotypically "evil". It really is just there to give the barest hint of context to the patterns of enemies coming at you. Thankfully, blowing stuff up was enough to overcome the horrible story.
Overall, a fun 8 hours or so. It's worth at most a buck though, wait for a sale (or a Humble Bundle or something).

Works pretty great. I've been using other versions of Sony VEGAS Pro for years and have noted that there are many features in Pro that I'm just not going to use or need. Never wanted to buy it because of the $400/500 price tag, but I wanted something that would work better than Windows Movie Maker. If you have also used VEGAS in the past, you'll likely be right at home. Masking is still a thing here, it's just not in an obvious place you might remember, it's no longer in the Pan/Cropping menu, and you can't use a Pen or Lasso tool, but by using a Cookie Cutter tool or the Mask Generator Video FX Plug-in, which may not float your boat. You can also use the "Compositing Parent/Child" button on the Video track head to adjust visibility of the video tracks in a masking technique of sorts. In my opinion, a masking Pen/Lasso tool alone is not worth $400. I want one, but I don't want one that bad.
Per YouTube's requirements, for those of you looking for good video editing software for your usual YouTube Let's Play videos, you can get 1080x60fps.mp4 files. While this software does mention it has exporting options for YouTube Facebook and Vimeo, it appears that using said options will produce a lower quality video ( an estimated 1 Gb video would be around 86 Mb using this feature) so I doubt I will ever use that, but I'm sure it must be useful to somebody.
Bottom line is, buy this, then delete any other version you
aqcuired because you wont need anything else. If you're looking to give this a test run, do it quick because rendering 10-minute 1080p videos will easily take 2 - 5 hours to complete and you'll have passed the point of no return before you know it.
If you're already using editing software you aquired from
questionable origin and you would like to something cheap and more legitimate, this is a good buy. If you're still using version 13 and you're absolutely fine where you're at, there's not likely a reason to upgrade unless you really just want to have the latest version.

To be honest, I sincerely enjoyed this game. Sure, there's butt-loads of text to read, but it's pretty much an interactive book. But, as it says in the game's description, it shows those who have depression that they aren't alone, and that there are easily accessible ways to find aid and assistance from their friends, family, and loved ones.

:The story was simply beautiful. The story continues directly after the first volume where the group is being confronted by Melano. The second volume shows the first part of the Viscanta arc where they met a tour guide named Sol, who is not what they think he is. Throughout the entire volume, there were two situations running along at the same time:
. Even though there were two issues happening concurrently, more empahasis was being placed onto the second one.
Ritona and Princess Selphine have been given more character development in this volume, although they still have the habit emphasising more of it to the newly introduced characters in the volume. There are times where the story is paced very slowly but they were used to fully bring out the inner thoughts and feelings of every characters in the situation. There was a point where Sol was trying to learn how to control the environment to allow a medicinal plant to grow. At that point, his emotional struggles with life was slowly revealed and although I cannot understand the kind of feelings he had, but I still felt that it was well written to show that the start of something new is never easy.
Another major character development shown in the volume comes from Princess Selphine. Princess Selphine pretty much disappears in the second half of the volume and is replaced with the personality of her ancestor, Queen Rhegan. Initially, Queen Rhegan is shown to be a ruthless warmonger but after several interactions with Sol's sister, she easily became my favourite character in this volume. Not only did she turn out to be an extremely wise and charismatic person who could create inspirational quotes in two-thirds of the sentences she says, she also has a caring side as well.
The reason why I said that this story is beautiful is because once again, they hit really hard at the feels towards the end just like what they did for the first volume.
One fault that I could possibly find in this story is the introduction of the trio who started their search for Ritona. While they desperately wants to track down Ritona and Princess Selphine and rescue them, I really doubt they would have any major plot significance in the series.
Fault Milestone 2 has really improved alot ever since the first volume. The artwork quality has improved and more animations have been added, What really impressed me the most was
.I look forward to more hand drawn scenes because I feel that these scene were the most beautiful.
Those who read Fault Milestone One must read this, they will blow your expectations away. Those who didn't can still take a look at the story but might struggle abit with unfamiliar terms. Don't make the mistake that I did of watching through youtube videos in the first volume, support the producers! I eagerly await for the third volume and the conclusion of the Viscanta arc. I also hope that they release a light novel adaptation and possibly an animation of this series.

I don't understand the thought process of this game.
1.)
The hidden orbs are not that well-hidden and the one-or-two puzzles that utilize the 2D design feel forced and unneeded when, you know, you could move around in 3D as an alternative.
The game has/is a 3D environment that wants you to imagine it's only 2D. Funny enough, when you zoom-out for viewing the room, the game looks and plays like a 2D-ish game.
(I'm not joking; there's a room at Level 14/15--I don't recall since they all blur into one--where each player is "trapped". Only, the forcefield blocks one part of the floor/screen when you could just walk around it, There's no facade.)
2.)
It's not that long of a wait, 10 to 15 mins at most, but it still makes no sense. Look at Forced, Ibb & Obb, Castle Crashers, etc.
3.)
I tried out cooperative with my significant other and we were doing the same thing I did for single-player: Waiting to advance based on the other player's involvement.
4.)
The game is far too short and takes way too long to get going on the cooperation (you two are only in the same room ONCE in my playthrough.) Not only does the game feel like a proof-of-concept of a game, there are tons of bugs and optomization problems (still). Thankfully the controller options work and the controls are fine.
5.)
If you were hopping for the Portal Coop Bots, think again. I just refer to them as the Suck Bot and the Boom Bot. That's all they do in the game, and there is no deviation or something to change up their mechanics.
You pick up boxes, you move them and suck up energy. (R3D)
You can't jump to save your life; you need R3D to give you a lift--with boxes--and the only fun you have is blowing stuff up, which can cause horrible screen-tearing effects. (BLU3)
6.)
. I'll be upfront and say that I haven't played the "Hard Mode" setting. But I fail to see how, when you beat the main-game, conserving your energy bursts will be any more challenging. There aren't alternative paths or extra obstacles designed to make you backtrack. The only challenge is not misfiring early too much, which I never had a problem.
7.)
Yes, there are small differences and sound-effects thrown in, sometimes, but it still sounds like the same song. (Where is that trailer song? I have not heard anything like it. Nor have I seen the cutscenes.)
8.)
You can run through the enemies and not worry, so long as you don't stay too long in the camera's spotlight or you remember to jump past a turret.
9.)
I played UP to chapter three and gave up because I didn't get one clue of context about who am I, what am I doing, why is everything trying to destroy me, and why should I care.

I must admit I haven't played the Steam version as much as the Desura version (I got it back in early 2014), but I'd recommend this game to all fans of introductory level strategy games. It's like a cross of Risk, Defcon and Command HQ (if anyone remembers that:
, seems to be available on Steam!). It's a simple World Conquest RTS with a limited number of units that all have the same strength, but different movement capabilities. In later scenarios you also get nuclear missiles that are extremely expensive but can wipe out whole stacks of enemy units.
Like Unity of Command it's easy to learn (although the controls can take some time to get used to since they're non-standard and were originally intended for controllers) but hard to master. It has a range of different scenarios of varying scope, that get more and more difficult. Some of them have randomized starting positions, so they play differently each time.
The AI is a pretty strong opponent, especially in the later scenarios. It can sometimes be a little passive though, especially when it doesn't have much ressources (some of the minor powers on bigger scenarios like the Pacific War scenario).
The Multiplayer scenarios that get unlocked during the course of the campaign are an addition to the Steam version, I can't comment on them yet.
If you like games like Command HQ, Defcon or Empire Deluxe, give it a try, you won't be disappointed.

This is an RTS game that has put together a lot of different aspects into one game. Will go over each side of the game one by one.
Gameplay:
The gameplay is fun without a doubt. I have enjoyed every minute of the game. I have seriously taken a lot of time in some missions just to decide on the country I would play in. It has different layers of strategy that you seamlessly get used to. The missions are well designed; though it is sad that they are actual wars in recent history. I could not try the co-op missions due to not being able to find a partner for a long time. AI is good and actually follows your movements and changes attacks which forces you to react accordingly.
Graphics:
There is not much in the sense of "graphics" in this game. It is more like a spherical Risk (boardgame) map. Units are representations and there is no animation. The day-night cycle and weather effects are good but it is just a flash thing. It actually bothers me that units have no animation but the sky is much more detailed.
Sound:
Oh God the voice of your computer assistant is really annoying! I had to shut her up in the third tutorial mission and just try to learn things on my own. Someone just reading the lines (just, anyone) would have been less annoying than this automated reading machine. The unit sounds are basic but gets the job done. Clicking sounds may annoy some people who give a lot of commands quickly but I doubt it will come to that in this game. The music is bad. Seriously in one mission a lady was just screaming an I waited for so long for a change in the tune or note or melody but no. That was shut down as well.
One important topic that I think needs special mention. You only use your mouse for all of the commands and it sometimes gets complicated and you might have to try 3-4 times before you can do what you want. I could not properly master it in 75 minutes, and I think adding some keyboard shortcuts can be easier (though I don't know for which command. Attack? Load/Unload?)
Overall this game is a really great idea just bogged down with technical difficulties. It is deep and requires a good deal of thinking. It would have been much better if the sound was not as annoying and you did nothave to wrestle with your mouse at a few points in the game. I would recommend the game with your own music in the background and a bit of patience to get used to the controls.

Grid 2 is Grid with some improvements, some fun removed, grind added and a much greedier eye on your wallet (DLC).
Positives:
It looks much better than the older Grid.  There are more different tracks.  There are disciplines with dynamic circuits, which forces you concentrate on the road ahead and controlling your vehicle instead of driving with one eye on a circuit map.  There are more different atmospheric conditions so you might find yourself dazzled by low sun, or struggling to pick your way through a twisty road at dusk or in the deep shade of a mountain and so on.  The car handling is something lots of people complain about but I like it a lot and think it's an improvement.  Different cars handle very differently and you do need to learn them and also try to pick one appropriate for the circuits in the series you are going to race.  I think the sound is good, an improvement over Grid and much more immersive.
Negatives:
The worst thing is the whiny doofus guide/commenter/whatever who just won't stop talking.  The few bits of important and helpful information he offers are lost in an ocean of boring, annoying, repetitive, trite, pointless drivel.  In the options you can switch him off almost completely.  I would have liked an option to tape his mouth shut and beat him.
Unfortunately you do kind of need to know some of what he says when you begin playing.  The fake ESPN type TV slots are 100% pointless, as tedious as hell and can't be avoided.  The game is horribly slow between events.  Too many events just seem to be there to make you grind your way through.  The reward at the end is to hear Mr Whiny Doofus whine some more while the game very sl o o o o w l y gets ready to offer you the next event.  It is very boring indeed waiting between events and when this is combined with non-optional boring events the whole things gets too annoying.  Too often you can't just game without numerous interruptions which kill the enjoyment.
In the original Grid there was a good system for setting the look and style of your vehicles' livery.  In Grid 2 it is much more limited and also harder to use.
Grid 2 has been infested with social media BS.  Instead of competing for cash and earning your progress with wins and buying your cars with game money you now earn fans and are occasionally shown inane social media style comments.  It's as uninteresting and brainless and poorly implemented as it sounds.

The saving grace is that the racing can be really enjoyable, enough so you might put up with all the bs, dumb efforts to get you to buy DLCs, filler events, and the dead minutes between racing.
With the original Grid I never quit the game out of boredom or irritation but with Grid 2 I find this happens too often.  I still play it but it can feel like a task, not a recreation.  Overall it's recommendable because the racing can be good, it does look great and these days it is often heavily discounted.  It absolutely is not worth the regular price.  I got mine for 25% of the regular price on a Humble Bundle offer and am happy with that.

What makes this game good isn't it's single player, which is basically Farcry 3 +1.  It could do a lot to improve the game, but instead it only adds a thin layer on top of it.  Some of the characters around you are funny, and it seems to be a bit better at creating characters I find interesting, rather then being surrounded by mopy emo people... for the most part.  It trys a little too hard though sometimes and instead delivers more hollywood characters then people I'd believe to be in a setting.  It might be a little too critical.  Also it has half the map locked away until you progress through half of the quests.
People also say the wild life is really super duper hard, and the bases are punishing, but they never really seemed like much of a challenge to me.  Bow + arrow + range & highground = undetected win on compounds (even the strongholds,) and the wildlife seem to just have more HP.  The rhinos are a bit hard and take a lot of punishment when you first go up against them, but after you realize how the AI works and how you can work around their attacks they become just as easy as everything else.
Now to the fun stuff.  It's a hell of a lot of fun doing co-op with another friend.  I was laughing almost the whole time as we did silly fun things.  It's the kind of co-op Farcry 3 should have had.  Take the map, take all the sub quests (not the main ones sadly) and have at with a friend.  It's a hell of a lot of fun.  What would make it better?  If the game basically did what diablo 2 did when adding another person into the mix.  Make more enemies spawn or make them harder, because in the end having a second player just makes opening up the map, or taking out outposts/strongholds easier.
However the fun isn't in the challenge it's in doing dumb stuff, and crashing in weird ways and killing both of you by maybe panicking and firing a rocket launcher at your feet.  It also opens up more dialogue from a character called Hurk, who is the character the person joining into the game will be.  Who is like the main character, but funny, has really great lines, and...... well..... really would have been more fun if he was the main character instead of the bumbling, want to help, coy Rambo mic kill everything.  Which is weird because why would Rambo be coy?
The single player campaign is nothing to write home about.  It's basically Farcry 3, and there is some nudity in the game but it doesn't really add much to the game other then "and then there were more painted boobies... and a very very very brief shot of your characters crotch," as opposed to when Farcry 3 used it to make a powerful statement.  So basically just expect more Farcry 3.  Yet when I played it with a friend and laughed for hours, and hours.
What does the game need?  In co-op I'd love it if I could just explore the whole entirety of everything on the games map instead of being restricted to half of the playing field because I didn't progress through the whole story.  Then allow me to reset the map so we can take those outposts all over again.  Also when outposts get attacked and I just walk away?  I should probably have to retake them instead of nothing happening which takes away from the tension of the event.  Maybe I don't want to save the outpost?  Maybe I want to go and bow the crap out of the guards who retook it?  Ever think of that Farcry4?  Anyways it's a solid game and I'd say play away.  It will be fun, but when you co-op that is when the game will really shine.

It has a nice classic feel to the gameplay and even the "story" though not so deep may gain some light affection from older audiences.  Through the game you play the role of the weapons controller for the main ship as it sets sail through various seas and channels as an onslaught of enemies try to take you down.  The enemy leader as many have pointed out will bring memories of Cobra Commander as your captain exchanges words with him.  All in all it kept me entertained and if by watching the video and looking at the screenshots it looks like something you could enjoy then go for it.
Gameplay Control Points:
1: You do not have to steer the ship, you only fire the main ship's weaponry. (Ammo recharges.)
2: As you progress through the game  abilities become available for purchase & use: Reload 1/mission I think, EMP as many as you own, and time slow which is also as many as you own.  Time slow drastically decreases game speed while increasing missile ROF, speed, and recharging.
3: You may unlock better ships with fuel from mission completions.
4: You may unlock support ships with fuel as well, these have 1-2 activatable weapons with a shots & time limit to them before they go into cooldown.
5: The controls are very simple and easy to use, I would recommend most people rebind them as they see fit.  The one trick to the game is strategic use of abilities and proper pacing and accuracy/leading of enemy targets when firing the weapons.

Ah Thief. A beloved franchise that is quite dear to my heart!  I'm a huge fan of the older Thief games, which I played multiple times over the years ever since the release of The Dark Project in 1999/2000 and I was quite excited to learn that a new Thief game was being made.
To put you into perspective, I was so happy that it got announced and confirmed that a new Thief game was being made and best of all, developed by the talented Eidos Montreal who made that great gem which is Deus Ex: Human Revolution, a prequel game set before the events of the older Deus Ex games. It was all raved and I did too, loved that game very much. They didn't messed up the story, continuity of the previous older Deus Ex classics. Eidos Montreal earned my deepest respects with that masterpiece! Sure, that game may not be better than the first Deus Ex, but it was the second best of that franchise.
Then, came the announce of "THI4F". At that time, not much was revealed but it was hinted to be a sequel to Thief: Deadly Shadows (Thief 3) so at that time, no big deal, I was quite excited! And then, silence... for a long time... until news arisen that the game was being, made into a "pseudo reinvention", not totally a reboot nor a remake; and especially not a sequel. "Pseudo" as this Thief game doesn't explain Garrett's origins and starts the game with him as being the super master thief around... Like it is a game that occurs in a different universe than the Thief Classics.
Now, I got worried... especially with the E3 2013 showing (lots of AI issues shown live)
Months later, I was beginning to be very concerned for this game. Why discarding the previous work of the franchise? Thief is a niche franchise and the fans holds dearly the past games! And once some scraps of info got revealed time to time, my concerns were completely justified. Bad news after bad news (QTE, Stephen Russell replaced, etc), I was getting so letdown by this new Thief game. I tried to be hopefull and even dared to PreOrder the game, to show my support to EM but alas, they really disappointed me badly with this product.
This Thief is not a mediocre game, it can be fun at times and many missions are reminescent to Thief 2 style. But for the true Thief fans from the original classic games, you will be VERY VERY dissappointed. This game doesn't really have the same ambiance of the classics. Benny's and taffer pals are gone, meaning no more humor between the guards. Citizens wandering around the city do not acknowledge you or even see you; giving them a robotic feel. The story is totally the biggest con of this Thief. It did everything to forget and distance itself from everything related to Thief Classics. In this new Thief, no more magic, supernatural elements are gone, THE CITY ain't steampunk anymore! And, what happened to the Hammers? The Pagans? Keepers? Trickster? Viktoria? What about Mechanist robots, Pagan creatures, Keepers, Gods? GONE!!! All discarded! Worse, your mechanist eye has different story and ain't even "mechanist" anymore but some bullcrap like "Primal", which explains the use of FOCUS function in the game; that highlights your surroundings / loots / traps to ease of your gameplay.
A big annoyance in this game (it is also present in many other games and I'm very annoyed by it) is the many contextual applied for this game. You have to watch Garrett steal and interact with everything as opposed to just taking things like the Thief classics. Why a problem? Well, it slows you down for crying out loud! I haven't really dabbled with the combat in this Thief since this game is all about being stealthy and not a tank warrior! From what I tried in the Master difficulty level, you die in two hits... so you better be good at dodging! Still, I'd say this combat system is more realistic and modern. The game offers 8 Chapters and about 30 side missions. There is also a challenge mode that you play a map of your choice, then try to accomplish a set count of challenges. It can be fun for a while but since the game only offer three maps now, it'll get stale fast!
Now, I will go with the pros and then, the long list of cons.
PROS:
+Stealth ambiance/atmosphere is there and mostly well done.
+Graphically/visuals impressive.
+Fun missions and many side missions.
+Custom options on your gameplay. Can disable HUD, Focus, etc. Lots of possible customizations!
+Upgrade system is kinda neat but also, weirdly implemented as your supposed to be THEE Master Thief!
+Swooping mechanic is neat and quite a blast to perform.
+Refined combat system compared to past Thief classics.
+Asylum level is tense, creepy at times too but short of being as scary as Thief 3: Deadly Shadows' Shalebridge Cradle level.
+Bank Heist DLC is very reminiscent of Thief 2 Bank mission. Highly recommended!
CONS:
-NO BENNY! NO TAFFERS!
-Stephen Russell, aka the voice actor of many characters on previous Thief games (Garrett, Benny, Karras, etc), was replaced by Romano Orzari; "a disconnect" the developers said but it was the developers who were disconnected from the true Thief genre. Full body motion technology was barely witnessed in-game so it was really a cheap excuse to dispose of Russell's that easily.
-A few stuttering issues, bugs and unstable at release. Mostly fixed by now though.
-Everything ignored on past Thief games except "Garrett, The City, Basso and Jenivere" names in this game.
-Old factions gone! No Hammerites, Mechanists, Pagans, Trickster.
-Mechanist Eye is gone and replaced by some "Primal" crap, which explains the FOCUS function if you enable/use it.
-Sandbox navigation system is bad in this game. You easily get lost and try to find the proper path for a side mission or main mission. There's many loading too in this game... way too many.
-Abysmal story. Lazy poor a$$ narrative writing.
-Way too many contextual situations. Like being forced to do the developer's desired action.
-Boring and uninspired NPCs.
-No Eric Brosius soundtrack composer. This Thief Luc St-Pierre composer ain't bad but no Brosius.
-You cannot jump at will, you cannot use your rope-arrows on any wooden surface but only the developers specified areas. Your "choke-arrow" (known as Gas Arrow on Thief classics) only "choke" the targets and do not render sleep.
-Buggy AI
-Sound propagation is messy and at many times, you either don't hear footsteps or door opening/closing. Also, there's sound clipping and repeated sentences.
-Forced boss fight. Sure you can run and escape but it is so tedious that doing the fight is just less of a hassle.
-Limited replay value.
-STILL NO BENNY!
OVERALL:
Thief is an okay stealth game but as a THIEF-based game, very bad. Lots of bad decisions during development. The developers kept telling about "a disconnect" between fans and them, well duh! You, Eidos Montreal, made many bad calls for this game and it shows. And actually, EM simply should have used another name and make their own stealth game instead of screwing the great masterpieces of the past. Why didn't they just created a new character instead of messing up Garrett? A big irritant is why oh why did they just ignored the fans feedback for their game? Fans knew what was correct and what wasn't, yet, EM gave the fans the middle finger!
RECOMMENDATION:
Honestly, the worst Thief game. If you loved the Thief classics, you won't love this one. You may enjoy parts of it like I did but still, you'll be very disappointed in this iteration of Thief. My best advice... either play the GOOD OLD Thief classics or if you seek a modern game, play Dishonored! Granted Dishonored is more action-oriented but you can choose to play as a ghost as well. As for this "THIEF", wait for a sale!
Eidos Montreal, you are big TAFFERS for screwing up this franchise!
RATING:
As a Stealth game: 6.0 / 10
As a Thief game: 5.0 / 10
FINAL:
5.5 / 10

Since the F2P launch, the amount of players have increased dramically. As you may know, this is a "moba" game, but it takes the arena in moba as its core gameplay. There are no minions, shopping, or level ups; it is purely Team Deathmatch with a little bit of "control the objective". There is another game mode which is much harder to explain, but the TDM is Battlerite's main gamemode. The game is very complex. Almost all the abilites are skill shots, and there are even two versions of the same ability. The game offers high skill ceilings and has a varity of champions to choose from. There is a trait system that allows to you pick "upgrades" for your champion's skills. This is aimed for players to create custom loadouts aganist certain matchups. The game is not p2w at all. The reward system features a loot box/chest that only offer cosmetics, so no gameplay advantages there except looking cool on the battlefield.
I play this game on the casual level. What I really love about this game is the short matches. There will be matches that will have 5 rounds (Win condition is 3 rounds), and those are the ones that I love the most. Sometimes I just keep queuing to play more matches beacause that game is that fun for me. There are also times when players leave in the middle of the match, which causes forfeits. This can be frustrating for both teams, as it ruins the match. The same applies to toxic players also so be mindful of that. Sometimes matchmaking isn't great, and your team team will not have a warrior or a support (the match can still be winable). Overall, I really enjoy the game despite its minor problems because this is the only MOBA I enjoy playing. The other traditional MOBAs lost my interest over time, and this one offers something brand new.  I highly recommend this game to anyone, and hope you enjoy it as much as I do.

You earn more coins buy simpy turning laps, but you earn more when setting fast laps.   So if you are within a certain percentage of the top time for the day, you are rewarded with coin.  This is all sorted and tracked via the easy to use, in-game leader board.  That said, earning coin is a bit of a grind at the beginning...not overbearing, but it pays to make smart purchases...you don't want to be short on cash when in need of some rain tires. :)

Advice for newbies:
For new players, concentrate on one car and get the top varient you can afford. The Pike, and Turin in my opinion are the most challenging to master especially on tight tracks. Good luck and remember to have fun, that is what's important.

I had this game on my wishlist for quite some time.  When I saw it on sale, I was very exctied, so I bought a copy for me and friend to play together.  I couldn't have been more excited to finally get a chance to sit down and play it.
Then, I finally tried it, and boy was I disappointed.
-I had to restart levels the first five times in a row because one of us either glitched through the floor, got stuck in a wall or ended up between some boxes or a shelf and couldn't jump out.
-The options menu is not well designed.  It started me in 1024x768 and I couldn't turn the sound down because the bar was underneath the words.   Then when I changed resolution, I could only click on the bar, so there was no fine adjustment.  It was either 1 or 10, couldn't set anything in between.

-The servers were very laggy, especially when looking at your partners screen.

Glitches and stuff aside, the game just isn't as fun as I was anticipating.  It has some cool mechanics, but in the end we just found ourselves bored quickly.  There doesn't seem to be any real story and the game just isn't that challenging to warrant wanting to continue playing.
I will give the game another try when it comes out of EA because I really want to like it, but my hopes are very low.

TL;DR: Amazing platformer with great potential and capable devs, playing co-op recommended.
The game is available in the Indie Gala Friday Special Bundle 16 at the time of writing (for another 14 days) and I would strongly recommend buying it.
According to the FAQ in the game hub only two people are working on this game which makes the game so much more impressive. Graphics are great, the gameplay fun and the puzzles interesting and somewhat reminiscent of Portal 2, just, you know, without portals. If you're an avid fan of the genre you will not have too much problems with most of the puzzles but still some are fairly challenging. If you have opportunity to play the game in co-op use it, it's implemented well and a lot more fun than singleplayer.
I have not yet completed the game (I'd estimate I'm at roughly two thirds) and I reckon it would take about 6-8 hours to complete the game at this stage. Don't forget that it's still in early access so it will most probably get quite a bit more content later.
Most of the achievements are somewhat easy to achieve, either through normal playing or a small effort but some are pretty hard (speedruns, completing the game without dying and the like).
The thing I like most about this game are the devs. Usually criticism or bug reports will be ignored, bugs stay in the game forever and sometimes games are completely unplayable. Threads in the game hub will not be answered for weeks and if they're answered it's usually not very helpful (looking at you Magicka 2). That's not the case here, the state of the game is great for an early access title, better than many other AAA games were and are, and the devs usually respond in about half a day, lots of the bugs getting fixed within a day or two.
Bottom line: if you like platformers give this one a try and support the amazing developers.

War, the Game takes strategy back to fundamentals. It doesn't give the user dozens of different options and force them to tackle complex systems. No, War is more elegant in it's execution and gives the player a limited scope, requiring them to use strategy to outthink their opponent rather than sneaking an attack by in a thousand layers of choices. Combat is abstract and requires the player to decide where to manuever and where to sacrifice.
One feature I like about War is that no unit is better than another. Each adds exactly the same combat strength to a battle, but each unit has a unique ability. Tanks are fast, whereas Infantry can hunker down in defence. Fighters are some of the most powerful units, but there are a few principle zones they are limited to due to air field access. Bombers have further range, but cannot be based on carriers.
All of this makes for a game that has the elegance of a game like chess or go. Highly reccomended for strategy fans.

First Impressions:
I'm not sure what to make of this yet.  On one hand, it's a cross between RISK (without the cards), DEFCON, and an RTS...all three of which appeal to me.  On the other, the controls take some getting used to.  For one, there's no way to create a selection box...instead, you click and hold the left mouse button and drag over the units you want to select.  There's also no way to build units without first finding and clicking the appropriate structure on the map...C&C and other RTSs have since graduated from that way of thinking with separate production menus tabbed by unit class appropriately.  There's also no skirmish that I can find, just premade scenarios with no indication as to their difficulty.  All of these things have the potential to frustrate new players as they did me.  Combat is simplistic (you watch them fight with no direct control over anything once the opposing forces overlap) and the units types just aren't varied enough to make a difference.
Overall, I neither like or dislike this game...it's just "OKAY".  Despite all of the above issues, I do find it to be intriguing and strategic when I find a scenario setup that appeals to me.  With that said, I wouldn't pay $10 for it, knowing what I know now.  Give me difficulty settings, implement a skirmish mode with custom setup options, and make the interface/controls more user-friendly, and I'll be happy to revisit the game and possibly give it a positive recommend.

Grid 2 is more fun than a sim, and as a bonus, it's spectacular to look at. The cars are approaching photorealism in a way, that makes it difficult to describe them without coming over all amateur Top Gear, and the tracks - including bleached Miami, crackling Chicago and atmospherically muted Paris - give a highly textured depth to each event. The game runs very smoothly at 1920x1080 with all graphics options turned up, never dropping below 60fps.
There's decent variety to Grid 2's grab-bag of events too, mixing up point-to-point races with closed road and track competitions and a handful of one-off promo events (like racing pickup trucks against the clock). What really keeps the experience fresh, though, is the admirably aggressive AI, which will happily shunt and nudge you cliffwards even on the medium difficulty setting. And, as a welcome counterweight, it will also make realistic mistakes itself.
It's no replacement for the game's 12-player online races (which have a separate, less annoying experience-point system) but it does ensure, that the singleplayer career is always a challenge and never a grind.
Grid 2 is an accomplished and visually strong racer let down only by a bafflingly lane Career mode narrative.

Bunny & Piggy is an adorable 2D platformer. Yes, the game is deceptively difficult, but it never felt unfair to me, which is my major complaint with most of the "challenging platformers" out there on the market. Levels also reset very quickly upon death, which helps to keep mistakes from feeling *too* punishing.
Add in the trading cards and a bunch of rare achievements and this game is a winner in my book. (Seriously, most of the achievements have a 2% acquisition rate or less).  To me, a price of $0.99 feels about right for this game, so if you're thinking about purchasing it you may want to wait for a coupon or a sale. Just make sure that you understand that this game is difficult. Bunny & Piggy may be a game with cute graphics, but it's far from a casual game.

Bunny & Piggy is a difficult 2D platformer that gave me cancer.
The game design itself actually isn't that bad, and it is exactly what it claims to be: a difficult 2D platformer.  The music for the game is also all right, except when you hear the same soundtrack 10 million times.
Now to the part that gave me cancer. There is a lag/delay on movement buttons, especially the jump button. I kid you not, it is like a half second delay. If you are going to make a difficult 2D platformer, WHY oh WHY would you make it stupidly harder by having a delay. Not only that, but each level is timed, so laggish/delayed movements makes it even harder. OH you thought that perhaps you could get used to it as you go through levels? WRONG, level 1 is already insanely hard.
I COULDN'T EVEN PASS LEVEL ONE without raging BECAUSE OF THIS MOVEMENT DELAY.
If the game fixes the delay, I will perhaps give it another shot, but as for now, it is simply just a bad and poorly made game.
Rating: 4.7/10
Recommend Price: $0.19 or below (and hope they fix this lag/delay)

Depression Quest continues to be the work of excellent members of the video game community and aptly portrays how it can feel to live with depression. The video game medium works well to demonstrate the ways in which one's life becomes closed off by self-deprecating emotions; watching your options become fewer as your mood reaches new lows is a simple way to express to anyone what many people know and feel. A minimal presentation and soundtrack pull you in, and the pointed, powerful writing keeps you playing. Playing may well be an inappropriate word, but for those who have not experienced depression or are unclear about how it affects those they love, this is the best chance to play at depression and, hopefully, come away with a greater understanding of it. This game and experience comes wholly recommended to anyone seeking that understanding.

I don't recommend playing this game if you've ever experienced depression - because it takes you back to a time that you never want to revisit. Maybe it's a good thing to revisit those times and see how you are now. But it is scary how well this game captures the life experience of depression.

This game displays the thoughts running throught the mind of  depressed twenty-something guy. It allows you to choose between several actions, and see how those actions affect his depression and his relationships. You can also backtrack from choices if you change your mind or want to see other outcomes. Its about twenty minutes of a quick story in which you gain a further understanding of the depressed mind. Definitely worth the time.
Most people here are missing the point of this game. It's not for fun, or to "make the guy happy". It's to understand the mindset of someone who is depressed. It gives good insight into what depression is like for those who have it. Depression is a tricky beast; its hard for those who don't have it to understand it, and thus we can do little to help our loved ones battle it. If you play this game, you will come out the other side with a better understanding of the game.
tldr: A game which can make you more aware of depression and gives a quick journey through a compelling story.

Thief isn't the masterpiece we hoped for but nor is it the disaster the gaming press would have you believe.
At every turn the game loves to remind you that you're not playing Thief: The Dark Project, or even Dishonored, what with its compact level design, intrusive transitional load screens, Garrett's inability to jump and mantle anywhere other than where the level designers say he should, the almost completely useless tools and arrows, a laughable upgrade system, etc. On top of all that we have a nonsensical narrative that lead writer Rhianna Pratchett disowned, an over reliance on chapter denouments that have Garrett running away from Michael Baysplosions, and evidence that the QA department were clearly testing another game entirely: guards get stuck on patrol routes, dialogue drowned out by music, sound samples misfiring all over the place, enemies three rooms away sounding like they're standing right next to you, etc.
And yet, amidst all this turbulence and chaos, there still lies a satisfying stealth experience. Levels show occasional flashes of inspired design, the use of light and shadows is frequently spectacular, the city itself is a wonderful labyrinth of streets, alleyways, courtyards, rooftops and secret passages, and many of the smaller, more tightly focused client missions outshine some of the larger narrative missions. Play on Master (or an even more challenging custom difficulty mode) with all the HUD elements, loot glint and quest markers turned off and you'll have a more rewarding experience than if you merely stick to all the default settings.
The best yardstick I can suggest to judge this game by is Thief: Deadly Shadows. This rebooted Thief is very much in the vein of Ion Storm's approach to the series rather than the Looking Glass-esque game most of us were hoping for. If you can tolerate Deadly Shadows, you can probably tolerate Thief. Just wait for a seasonal sale if you still have your doubts.

"Do you recommend this game?"  Barely.  Despite a bevy of complaints, I still find it hard to pick either way.  I did enjoy playing it for a solid 40 hours.  On the other hand, I came away from it very disappointed.  It plays like a Thief game.  It sounds like a Thief game.  It doesn't FEEL like a Thief game, though.  I'll explain why in a moment but let me get to the good points first.  Oh and by the way this will be full of spoilers.
The sneaking and actual gameplay is great.  Most levels were actually surprisingly tricky to sneak through unnoticed.  But there was always a way.  I must've replayed most sections at least a few times trying to get it just right.  Figuring out those situations was quite satisfying.
Two levels in particular
affected me quite a lot.  One was marvelously creepy and scary with tons of great moments.  The other was just a joy to wander through and wonder at the mystery of it all.  And it helped that both levels were quite nostalgic of great moments/themes in past Thief games.
And one more good thing I can say is that, taken on its own merits, I think the story in this game wasn't terrible.  I almost cared about it at times.  And it definately had me wondering where it would go next... I kept playing just to see if the great potential of it all would pan out.  Their were certainly some fantastic opportunities for some really classic revalations to be made...
...which the writers/devs completely failed to take advantage of.  That's the first of my complaints.  The story overall does fall flat in the end.  And speaking of the ending, it's one of the worst I've seen in a while.  They tried to make it artsy, which some may appreciate.  However....

Looking back at the game in general, none of the interesting personality of past Thief games is there.  This I believe is probably because
There's guards, but they're not anywhere near as interesting to listen to.  And they repeat their lines way way way too often for how dull they are.  I miss the oafish buffoon guard complaining that he'd rather be at a bear baiting.
The side missions are mostly useless time-fillers that are there just to let you earn some money without actually providing any interesting content.  The environments look beautiful but nothing feels lived in.  There's plenty of books to pick up and read, but doing so opens an extremely basic, minimal text menu.  With all the beautiful modelling, texturing and animation in the game... why not show me reading an actual book?  Immerse me in the world more!  Don't remind me I'm playing a video game by showing me a menu unless I'm trying to change video settings or something.
I very nearly didn't recommend this game, for all these reasons.  Particularly for the horrendous ending.  You never want to end a game like this with a, "WTF, that's it?!?"  Honestly, I think that kinda ruined the game for me.  But the more I think back on it, the more I can see that I did enjoy the majority of the time I spent actually playing it.  Particularly because the missions were challenging to perfect.  Given some time I could see myself going back and having a bit of fun knocking out the few achievements and secrets I missed.  But I'd also be disappointed again by all the wasted potential and lost opportunities for a game that could've been truely great.

Let's talk about what's good first
The atmosphere of this game alone is an experience that makes the game worth playing. I'm a fan of stealthy games and right out of the gate I was just blown away by the visuals. Controls were solid, allowing all that you'd expect from a master thief. For those who compare it to Dishonored, the art, animation, ability balance are flat out better. I found even the RPG elements to be much better thought out here.

You're a sneak but you're not penalized for going all kung fu on a guard if that's what you need to do to avoid being caught. The light crystal was a good idea as sometimes shadows aren't all as shadowy as you think they are, while other times you are invisible right beside a guard.
The puzzles were fairly puzzling at times which is good, there's nothing worse than a game where they show you the solution to everything you're supposed to 'figure out' on screen. That's what Google is for baddies ;)
Now for the bad
Loading screens. Lots of loading screens. It seemed like the windows you have to pry open every few steps and narrow crawl ways would give ample time to load the next area without having to pause as well. I really get the feeling that was the idea to begin with but the game was rushed to be an early 'next gen' title.
The story starts out absolutely great, pulling you in from the get go and then... goes nowhere. Things make no sense, characters don't get fleshed out, cliches get abused, it's just badly written dialog and you can't blame the voice actors. I honestly don't know why there are prerendered cutscenes in the game, the hardware rendered scenes are so much better. It's strange to go to a blurry video when the engine itself can handle better graphics. Again, a lot of signs of rush, some cuts between scenes are so abrupt that you wonder what just happened. Sucks that this game is going to keep being compared to Dishonored, but Dishonored did it better.
Potential spoiler, but midway through the game there's a certain level that suddenly switches the game from being about steath to being horror. While I found it interesting to experience, I'm not particularly a fan of horror games and back to back jump scares. I missed most of the level I would've liked to have explored more, only without something leering in my face screaming at me.
Finally, despite all the collections and really expensive items, there's not a lot of replay value. Once the main story is wrapped up, there's little reason to stick around unless you just have to have those achievements. If that's you, read up on the game ahead of time, because many will likely be blocked to you unless you play the whole thing again.

Short summary of cons and pros.
Pros:
+Easy to use.
+Easy to learn how to use it.
+Not expensive.
+License included to monetize finished product.
+Additional functions you might add using iscript and Tyranoscript.
Cons:
-No samples for backgrounds, music or characters included. So if you have no own skill to create those by yourself by    using other softwares like Musicmaker, Photoshop or GIMP etc..., you might have a problem.
Impression:
This software sounds like a dream for those people out there that wanna try themselves as a novel game creator.
This software includes all the basic functions to create a novel game, plus that you can implement some of your extra needs through the use of scripts.
The UI is self explaining for those who have at least some basic knowledge about nowadays softwares, but even if not, I think it's quite simple to learn how to use this software, since you don't really have to do all the programmings by your self.
So how does it all work?
First of all, you should prepare some basic materials for your novel, such as Background pictures, Background music and character pictures.
Since you can't adapt them in this software, you have to do all the adjustment work etc by using other softwares like Photoshop etc...
So if you think you gonna need the same character in different sizes, you should also prepare those in different sizes.
If you don't have the skill to make these materials by yourself, you could also use materials found on the internet, but beaware, since this might cause a lot of copyright issues if you aren't carefull.
So if you are planning to distribute it on the internet, that's going beyond the line of private usage, you better be sure to use only your own original creation in it.
Once the materials are ready, you can now add them to the software.
Now in the softwares UI, you will see a flowsheet of events, such as changing backgrounds, characters entering the scene, writing texts or changing the music etc.
Now you can drag and drop the event of your choice, let's say character enters a scene for example, to the right place where you want it to happen, then chose the character from a list of all characters that are added to the software already, then you can adjust this character's position on the screen,
Now drag and drop the event "text" right after this, and write "Hello", to have a scene where your character enters the scene and says "Hello".
All other functions like changing background, changing or stopping music, using special effects will work like this by drag and drop, and then choosing what happens specifically.
Of course you also have the options to adjust the screen size, fontstyle, position of the text window etc etc....,
You can always preview all the work done by now, by simply clicking on the preview button, to check for bugs etc.
When you are done, so when your game is finished, all you need to do is to export the gamefiles to your PC folder.
When exporting the file you can chose for what platform you might export the file, like browser game, Windows app,  Mac app, iOS app or Android app.
Well there are some features that I couldn't find out if they exist like, adding charachter voices besides the BGM, or how to make the game (not the software) to run in fullscreen.
Maybe these can be done only by scripting it, but I am not really sure about that.
As you can see, it's all quite simple.
I'm sure creating a full novel game will consume a lot of time, but I think this software is good to help you shorten that time, and will drastically simplify your work.
Totally worth it's price, so, a clear recommandation to all the upcoming novel game creators of tomorrow!

They said it was easy to use and it 100% is! TyranoBuilder makes game design programs such as RPG Maker look like complex programming. (And if you've used RPG Maker you'll know it is fairly easy to learn!) Tyranobuilder is a perfect place to start if you want to begin making games. It is easy and fun to use.
Now, I was a little worried about there being no prerendered art or resources included with this program, but it turned out to not be a problem at all. If you aren't planning on selling your games you can find thousands of free resources--character sprites, backgrounds, music, etc--online. And if you want to create games to sell on the market it is worth it to do the drawing yourself--even fun! Some artists even allow you to use their work in your commercial games as long as you credit them--but make sure to always ask permission first!
If you are a fan of visual novels, anime, or just plain old storytelling you're goint to love this program! TyranoBuilder is the best purchase I've ever made on steam. (Right next to RPG Maker VX Ace!)
